title: Signature Deletion Certificates
description: Signature edition: every sanitization issues a deletion certificate — what was deleted, which technique, when, verified by what check. Certificates are the audit trail proving 'gone means gone' — compliance and forensics both consult them. This is a Signature original method.
method: Issue certificates per deletion with (target, technique, verification); store tamper-evidently; present on audit.
usage: Require certificates for regulated data; verify a sample independently.

demo.code:
cert = {'target': 'session keys', 'technique': 'zeroization', 'verified': 'memory scan clean'}
print('deletion certificate:', cert)

title: Signature Secure file deletion
description: Signature edition: Deleting a file usually just unlinks it — the bytes remain on disk until overwritten. Secure deletion overwrites content before unlinking (multiple passes per DoD 5220.22-M historically; single pass suffices on modern drives), and on SSDs uses ATA Secure Erase or crypto-shredding since overwrites don't reliably reach flash cells.
method: Overwrite file content, then unlink; on SSDs prefer crypto-shredding (destroy the key) or ATA Secure Erase.
usage: Encrypt sensitive files at rest (then deletion = key destruction); never rely on unlink alone.

demo.code:
print('sensitive.tmp: overwrite with random (1 pass), then unlink')
print('SSD: crypto-shredded (key destroyed) -> unrecoverable')

title: Signature Forensic recovery resistance
description: Signature edition: Against forensic recovery, deletion must consider remapped sectors, wear leveling, and filesystem journals — all places 'deleted' bytes survive. Resistance means layered deletion (overwrite + crypto-shred + secure erase) matched to the medium, verified by attempting recovery in test.
method: Layer techniques per medium; attempt forensic recovery in test; close the gaps the recovery finds.
usage: Test deletion by trying to recover; assume the adversary has your test lab's tools.

demo.code:
print('deletion test: forensic scan of wiped drive')
print('recovered: 0 sensitive bytes -> RESISTANT')

title: Signature Log sanitization
description: Signature edition: Logs are where secrets go to live forever: passwords in URLs, tokens in headers, PII in debug output. Sanitization means structured logging with field-level redaction — secrets never enter the log pipeline, and patterns (credit cards, tokens) are scrubbed even from free text.
method: Structured logs; redactlist for sensitive fields; regex scrubbing for free text; review log samples for leaks.
usage: Redact at the logging call site; scrub defensively downstream; audit samples regularly.

demo.code:
import re
log = 'user login token=abc123-secret'
clean = re.sub(r'token=\S+', 'token=[REDACTED]', log)
print('sanitized log:', clean)

title: Signature Ephemeral key exchange (PFS)
description: Signature edition: Perfect forward secrecy uses ephemeral keys per session (ECDHE): even if the long-term key is later compromised, past sessions stay secret because their keys were ephemeral and destroyed. PFS is sanitization built into the protocol — session data self-destructs by design.
method: ECDHE key exchange per session; destroy ephemeral keys after use; never log session keys.
usage: Require PFS cipher suites; verify ephemeral keys are actually destroyed.

demo.code:
print('session: ECDHE ephemeral keys -> destroyed after handshake')
print('long-term key later stolen: past sessions STILL SECRET (PFS)')

title: Signature Data retention policies
description: Signature edition: The policy layer: what data lives how long, who approves exceptions, and how deletion is verified. Retention schedules (30 days for logs, 7 years for financials) plus automated enforcement turn 'delete old data' from intention into operation — sanitization at organizational scale.
method: Define retention per data class; enforce automatically; approve exceptions explicitly; audit compliance.
usage: Write the schedule down; automate enforcement; audit exceptions.

demo.code:
policy = {'debug logs': 30, 'access logs': 90, 'financials': 2555}  # days
print('retention schedule:', policy)
print('enforcement: auto-delete on expiry, exceptions need approval')

title: Signature Swap and hibernation protection
description: Signature edition: Secrets in RAM can leak to disk via swap or hibernation files. Protection means locking sensitive pages (mlock/VirtualLock) so they never swap, and encrypting hibernation images — defense for the data's entire lifetime, including when the machine sleeps.
method: mlock sensitive buffers; encrypt swap or disable it for secret-handling processes; encrypt hibernation images.
usage: Lock key material in RAM; treat hibernation files as sensitive; audit swap configuration.

demo.code:
print('mlock(key_buffer): pages locked, never swapped')
print('hibernation image: encrypted -> secrets safe while asleep')

title: Signature Crypto-shredding
description: Signature edition: The elegant deletion: encrypt everything with per-object keys, and 'delete' by destroying the key. Ciphertext without the key is random noise — instant, verifiable, and works on any storage medium including SSDs and backups (as long as keys aren't backed up with the data).
method: Per-object data keys; destroy the key to delete; verify no key copies survive (HSM, backups, logs).

specification.caveat: keys must not be backed up

usage: Design for crypto-shredding from the start; manage key lifecycle rigorously.

title: Signature TTL-based auto-expiry
description: Signature edition: Ephemeral data should die on schedule: TTLs on cache entries, self-destructing messages, auto-expiring tokens. The system, not human discipline, enforces deletion — data that can't linger because its lifetime is structural, not procedural.
method: Set TTLs at creation; enforce expiry in the storage layer; sweep expired data on schedule; log deletions.
usage: Default to short TTLs for sensitive temporaries; make 'forever' require justification.

demo.code:
import time
cache = {'token': (12345, time.time() + 300)}
val, exp = cache['token']
print('token valid:', time.time() < exp, '(auto-expires in 5 min)')
